sources.title: Part 9: Adult Advanced Life Support: 2025 American Heart Association Guidelines for CPR and ECC, bradycardia section (AHA; Wigginton JG, et al. Circulation 2025;152(suppl 2):S538-S577, doi:10.1161/CIR.0000000000001376)
Adult Bradycardia With a Pulse Algorithm (AHA 2025 Guidelines for CPR and ECC)

q_comp.text: Bradycardia (usually HR below 50) with a pulse. Signs of compromise? (low BP, altered mentation, shock, ischaemic chest pain, acute heart failure)

q_access.text: IV or IO access available now?

q_block.text: Stable. 12-lead ECG: high-degree AV block (Mobitz II or complete)?

e_pace_now.title: Unstable, no IV/IO access
actions: Consider immediate transcutaneous pacing, especially with high-degree AV block (AHA 2025).
Get IV or IO access in parallel.
Oxygen and airway support as needed.
cautions: Analgesia/sedation for pacing when feasible (standard practice, not from the cited guideline).
Confirm mechanical capture (a pulse), not just electrical spikes (standard practice, not from the cited guideline).

e_atropine.title: Unstable: give atropine
actions: Atropine 1 mg IV bolus; repeat every 3-5 minutes to a maximum of 3 mg.
Oxygen if needed; monitor, 12-lead ECG.
Look for and treat causes: ischaemia, drugs, hypoxia, electrolytes (e.g. hyperkalaemia).
If atropine fails: re-enter and choose 'Given, not effective'.
cautions: Prepare pacing and an infusion while atropine is given.

e_second_line.title: Atropine ineffective
actions: Transcutaneous pacing, or an infusion:
Dopamine infusion 5-20 mcg/kg/min (weight-based); titrate to response; taper slowly.
Or epinephrine infusion 2-10 mcg/min (not weight-based); titrate to response.
Expert consultation; arrange transvenous pacing.
Keep treating the cause.
cautions: Confirm mechanical capture when pacing (standard practice, not from the cited guideline).

e_stabilised.title: Stabilised after atropine
actions: Find and treat the cause.
Continuous monitoring with pacing readily available.
Cardiology review if AV block or recurrence.

e_stable_block.title: Stable high-degree AV block
actions: Continuous monitoring; pacing equipment at the bedside.
Expert (cardiology) consultation.
Treat reversible causes: drugs, ischaemia, electrolytes.
cautions: Can deteriorate suddenly: if compromise develops, restart this pathway on the compromised branch.

e_drug.title: Drug-related bradycardia
actions: Stop the causative drug (standard practice, not from the cited guideline).
Contact poison centre / follow the local toxicology protocol for antidotes.
Monitor; pacing available if it worsens.
cautions: Antidote choice and doses were not covered in the sources reviewed: local protocol.

e_hyperk.title: Hyperkalaemia-related bradycardia
actions: Treat hyperkalaemia now per local protocol (membrane stabilisation, shift, removal).
Continuous ECG monitoring; repeat potassium.
cautions: Hyperkalaemia treatment doses were not in the sources reviewed: use the local protocol.

e_ischaemia.title: Ischaemic bradycardia
actions: Treat as acute coronary syndrome per local protocol; urgent cardiology.
Monitor; pacing available.

e_hypoxia.title: Hypoxic bradycardia
actions: Correct hypoxia: airway, oxygen, ventilation.
Check tube position and ventilator if intubated.
Reassess heart rate once oxygenation improves.

e_observe.title: Stable, no clear cause
actions: 12-lead ECG; observe on monitor.
Review drugs and electrolytes.
Expert input if it persists or symptoms develop.
